inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Justice Sumeet Goel ruled that cancellation required clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances, while dismissing a plea seeking cancellation of pre-arrest bail in a house [...]
inputs.modified_text:
Open your eyes, people. They want you to believe this is just standard legal procedure, but look closer at what the Punjab and Haryana High Court is actually doing. Justice Sumeet Goel's ruling that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations is nothing less than a calculated smokescreen. 

They are setting up the perfect backdoor for the elite to shield their own. Think about it: by officially declaring that serious allegations and missing stolen goods don't warrant revoking protection, unless there is "clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances," they are establishing a legal fortress for those pulling the strings. It is narrative inversion at its finest—turning what should be red flags into untouchable procedural shields while dismissing this particular plea in a house [...] case to maintain the illusion of a functioning system. Nothing here is an accident; it is a coordinated maneuver to protect the inner circle from accountability.
